prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Scope: checked baggage from bag-drop/transfer induction through screening, sorting, make-up, handoff at outbound load control point; excludes aircraft loading. Elements: - Pier 4 Bag-Drop Unit: records accepted bags; sends Oversize Exception Ticket. - Bag Tag Printer: unique tag per bag; produces Calibration Witness Tag when calibration witness record required. - Transfer Bag Feeder: identifies transfer bags; sends Late Transfer Bag Card; holds transfer bags until screening status/onward handling confirmed. - Induction Tray Conveyor: controlled feed, spacing for image capture and identification before route selection. - Baggage Control System (Velvet): links tag to passenger/flight record; validates transfer routing; applies screening profile; loads approved sort plan with effective time window before sortation; checks plan vs flight/handling records before assigning route; routes exception bags to Secondary Inspection Chute. - Concourse Zone Controller (Mosslight): produces Recovery Route Card; grants induction permissive; coordinates conveyor availability with sort plan. - Flight Data Gateway (Lantern): sends Flight Cutoff Advisory; supplies flight/routing records. - North Gate Scanner (Kestrel), South Gate Scanner: read/verify bag identity at entry/route decision points, acquire images, return disposition; South produces Manual Rescan Receipt. - Primary Crossbelt Sorter (Juniper): applies destination and screening status per bag; sends Chute Occupancy Note when lane nears limit. - Image Resolution Desk: staff review images, record disposition. - Secondary Inspection Chute: occupancy-monitored, access restricted to authorized personnel. - Bag Reconciliation Station: verifies bag matches screening record. - East/West Make-Up Conveyors; Carousel 7 Make-Up Unit (Orchard): accepts only bags with valid disposition and authorized routing; Outbound Load Control Desk. Actors: Baggage Operations Supervisor (flight readiness, staffing, lane decisions; notified of isolation); Explosives Response Team (Pebble; escalated alarms, safety controls with airport security); Security Duty Manager (notified for beyond-routine security decisions); Maintenance Technician; Airline Ramp Coordinator (Carousel Release Slip); check-in/inspection staff. Requirements: verify eligibility before acceptance; hold bad-data/oversize bags; pre-induction checks; interlocks stop feed on jam/door/downstream loss; alarmed bags kept under control until authorized disposition; return to normal only when identity, outcome, routing consistent; route selection favors approved path with capacity and time.

New part:
S088: A scan mismatch prevents the bag from continuing on a route that depends on the unresolved identity.
S089: Congestion awareness uses current lane availability, conveyor stops, and the observed rate of incoming bags.
S090: The Baggage Operations Supervisor sets local congestion thresholds and confirms the authorized response to sustained overload.
S091: Tern is the operational alias used for the Baggage Operations Supervisor in sortation coordination.
S092: When a planned lane is unavailable, the Baggage Control System selects an approved alternate route only if screening status and flight timing remain valid.
S093: Bags with an unresolved destination or a route outside their handling limits are diverted to the Secondary Inspection Chute.
S094: The Image Resolution Desk resolves image-related holds before affected bags are returned to normal sortation.
S095: The Explosives Response Team manages security holds under the applicable response procedures.
S096: A bag returns to normal handling only after its identity, examination outcome, and routing authorization agree.
S097: The East Make-Up Conveyor and West Make-Up Conveyor are selected according to the active plan and available capacity.
S098: The Carousel 7 Make-Up Unit operates within its assigned flight window and reports when its usable capacity is constrained.
S099: The Transfer Bag Feeder continues to hold transfer bags until screening status and intended onward handling are confirmed.
S100: The Bag Reconciliation Station compares bag identity with the active handling record and flags unresolved discrepancies.
S101: The Bag Reconciliation Station sends a Bag Match Query when bag identity cannot be reconciled with the active handling record.
S102: Bags found on a stopped or misdirected path are held from onward movement until their location and identity are established.
S103: The Maintenance Technician isolates a failed conveyor section and confirms that the route is safe before service resumes.
S104: The Baggage Operations Supervisor authorizes recovery to the approved sort plan after the cause of the abnormal path has been addressed.
S105: Flight Data Gateway maintains scheduled flight identifiers, destinations, planned departure times, and revisions needed for baggage planning.
S106: Flight schedules include airline-specific dispatch targets and connection windows, and changes are time-stamped for operational use.
S107: Baggage Control System evaluates flight assignments against current schedule data before accepting bag routing instructions.
S108: The planned dispatch time is the reference for prioritizing bags, while the published departure time remains the passenger-facing schedule value.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
response:
{"summary":"Scope: checked baggage from bag-drop/transfer induction through screening, sorting and make-up to handoff at the outbound load control point; aircraft loading is excluded.

- Outbound Load Control Desk.
